How to Address the Planning Commission
Any person who would like to address the Planning Commission regarding an item on the
agenda, please fill out a Speaker's Form and submit it to the Deputy Clerk prior to the
agenda item you would like to discuss. You may address the Planning Commission once
per meeting, per public comment section of the agenda on only those matters within the
Commissioner's jurisdiction. Please note that you are not required to complete this form
or state your name and residence in order to speak. Each person addressing the
Planning Commission is given up to three minutes to speak (with double the time allotted
to non-English speakers using a translator). The amount of time authorized may be
adjusted by the chair. If you wish to provide information to the Planning Commission,
please present the Deputy Clerk with 7 copies. Otherwise, your materials will simply be
added to the administrative record. Please note use of City Council Chamber technology
equipment to present electronic material during meetings is not allowed.

In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-
related modification or accommodation to participate in this meeting, please contact the
City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. If you require
oral Spanish translation, please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-5151 at least
72 hours prior to the meeting.

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Nemeth called the meeting to order.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE TO THE FLAG

  Chair Nemeth led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Chair Nemeth; Vice Chair Henderson; Commissioners Alvarez, Elize, and,
  Fraga-Saenz

  Absent: None

4.  REVIEW OF AGENDA

  Chair Nemeth noted that item 9 will be moved up to follow the review of agenda
  item 4.

  Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Megan Taggart noted
  memorandums related to items 7A, 8A and 8B were provided prior to the meeting.
  The memorandums addressed minor typographical errors and modified a Condition of
  Approval within item 8A.

9.  PRESENTATION

  Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Taggart announced that
  this will be Chair Nemeth’s last meeting and would like to take the opportunity to thank
  her for her years of service and allow time for presentations from the local elected
  officials.

  Vice Chair Henderson presented a Commendation and gift on behalf of the City of
  Palmdale Planning Commission.

  Field representatives on behalf of Senator Scott Wilk, Assemblyman Tom Lackey and
  District 34 and Assemblyman Juan Carrillo District 39 presented a certificate of
  recognition to Chair Nemeth.

  Field representative on behalf Edwards Airforce Brigadier General Matthew Higer and
  Helida Vanhoy Director of STEM presented a certificate of recognition to Chair
  Nemeth.

  Juan Blanco on behalf of Coffee 4 Vets for the presented a certificate of recognition to
  Chair Nemeth for her volunteer work during the Edwards Airforce Airshow October
  2022.

7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

7A.  Approval of Minutes for the Planning Commission Meeting of February 9, 2023.

  Motion:  Approval of Minutes for the Planning Commission Meeting of
  February 9, 2023, as amended.
  Moved by Vice Chair Henderson, seconded by Commissioner Fraga-Saenz.
  Vote: Motion carried 5-0.
  Yes: Chair Nemeth; Vice Chair Henderson; Commissioners Alvarez, Elize and

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

8A.  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC-2023-006; a Resolution of the
  Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale, approving Tentative Parcel Map 83940
  and Site Plan Review 22-017; a request to subdivide approximately five acres into
  three lots for the purpose of constructing two restaurant buildings with drive-through
  facilities totaling 5,600 square feet located at the northwest corner of Rancho Vista
  Boulevard and Town Center Drive and finding that the project is consistent with the
  previously adopted Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and
  Reporting Program, as amended.

  Assistant Planner Sam Dominguez presented the item.

  Chair Nemeth asked City Traffic Engineer Jay Nelson to clarify how this project was
  deemed viable as it relates to traffic given the close proximity of the two drive-throughs.

  City Traffic Engineer Nelson stated the City required the developer to submit additional
  studies related to traffic counts and clarified that these studies, in addition to the
  conditions of approval are sufficient and determined the project is adequate for
  approval.

  Chair Nemeth opened the Public Hearing on this item.

  Chris Sizz of First Street Development represents the applicant and prospective
  tenants and made himself available for questions.

  Vice Chair Henderson asked questions regarding the circulation of drive-throughs
  related to the new Zoning Ordinance requirements for Parcels 1, 2 and 3 and

  @BCL@BC09DD21.docx  2
 expressed concerns related to traffic overflow. He noted Parcel 3 has more
opportunity to ensure proper circulation for traffic flow and is not concerned with
Parcel 3.

Chris Sizz addressed Vice Chair Henderson related to Parcel 2 that will be utilized as a
pick up lane only. The menu board will be removed to reflect the lane will only be used
for pickup mobile orders.

Vice Chair Henderson expressed his concern related to Parcel 2 and asked if
conditions of approval specifically state that this is for a pick up lane only for mobile
drive-through orders and if it can later be modified should there be a new tenant that
operates more like a typical drive-through.

Chris Sizz answered that is not anticipated to change.

Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Taggart confirmed staff
was not aware this had been changed to be a mobile pick up lane only. There is no
specific condition related to that.

Resident Eman Younan spoke in opposition to the project due to traffic congestion and
asked the Planning Commission to reconsider the approval of the project.

Chair Nemeth closed the Public Hearing on this item.

Commissioner Alvarez asked if there have been any studies of past practices in regard
to traffic control related to these types of projects to ensure safety for future projects.

Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Taggart answered
Commissioner Alvarez and stated staff evaluates each project on a case to case basis
related to specific drive-through development standards and require that queuing
studies be provided to analyze other locations to demonstrate they will be sufficient to
the use.

Commissioner Alvarez asked how the 500 foot distance requirement is being
considered for this project.

Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Taggart stated this project
is in a specific plan area governed by its own development standards and the Zoning
Code update has not been adopted by City Council yet and would not go into effect
until 30 days after their approval. This application would not be subject to that
particular requirement of the update.

Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-006, as amended.
Moved by Dean Henderson, seconded by Christina Fraga-Saenz.
Vote: Motion carried 5-0.
Yes: Chair Nemeth; Vice Chair Henderson; Commissioners Alvarez, Elize and
Fraga-Saenz.

 8B.  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC-2023-005; a Resolution of the
  Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale, approving Tentative Parcel Map 83984,
  Conditional Use Permit 22-014 and Site Plan Review 22-020; a request to subdivide
  one parcel into eight parcels for the purpose of constructing three commercial buildings
  and establish a tobacco/smoking retailer totaling approximately 11,305 square feet on
  a portion of a vacant approximately 10-acre parcel located at the northwest corner of
  Palmdale Boulevard and 5th Street West and find that the application is consistent with
  Environmental Impact Report 90-1 (SCH No. 89090618), which was prepared for the
  Palmdale Trade and Commerce Center Specific Plan and certified by the City Council
  on May 24, 1990 (Resolution No. CC 90-142) (APN: 3004-004-025), as amended.

  Acting Planning Manager Brenda Magaña presented this item and made herself and
  the applicant available for any questions.

  Chair Nemeth asked if we have many 24 hour convenience stores in our community.

  Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Taggart confirmed that
  there are some 24 hour establishments and that the Palmdale Municipal Code does
  not currently regulate, nor does it include hours of operation.

  Chair Nemeth opened the Public Comment on this item.

  Ralph Deppisch representing Sage Investco made himself available for any questions.

  Vice Chair Henderson asked regarding the EV parking spaces and whether they will
  be available to patrons as charging stations.

  Ralph Deppisch stated that per the new ordinance there is a minimum percentage
  requirement that must have the ability to provide a charging station in the future.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-005, as amended.
  Moved by Christina Fraga-Saenz, seconded by Getro Elize.
  Vote: Motion carried 5-0.
  Yes: Chair Nemeth; Vice Chair Henderson; Commissioners Alvarez, Elize and
  Fraga-Saenz.

10.  STAFF COMMUNICATIONS

  Deputy Director of Economic and Community Development Taggart noted the tentative
  agenda has been provided for the April 13, 2023, meeting. In addition, she also
  announced she has taken on a new position with the City, Brenda Magaña is the
  Acting Planning Manager and introduced the new Land Use Attorney, Alex Halfman of
  Harper and Burns.

 11.  PLANNING COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Commissioner Fraga-Saenz announced the 11-day Clean California Event in
  partnership with Caltrans will be held Saturday, March 25th on Ave O between 10th
  Street West and Division St. Everyone is welcome. She also announced this is
  tentatively her last meeting as Planning Commissioner.

  Commissioner Alvarez commended Commissioner Fraga-Saenz for her clean-up
  efforts.

12.  ADJOURNMENT TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING OF THURSDAY,
